input: A completed TypeScript change contains two identical private helpers, one unused import, and a loop that manually performs a supported Array method. The focused tests pass.
expect: The agent runs the focused tests first, removes the unused import, merges the repeated helper logic, uses the supported clear native method, then runs the same tests and relevant formatter and static checks. The report names structural reductions rather than only a line count.

input: A named Rust scope has a private helper called parse_customer_policy that is called once. Inlining it saves five lines but hides the domain operation inside a long match expression.
expect: The agent keeps the helper because its name preserves a domain concept and inlining harms readability. The report lists it under Kept. No line-count target overrides that decision.

input: The target tests fail before any simplify edit because the fixture cannot connect to its test database.
expect: The agent stops without editing code and reports the exact baseline command and failure. It does not infer that the proposed reductions are safe and does not run an after result as if it were comparable.

input: A request handler checks that a decoded JSON field is present, although the internal typed object marks the field as required. External clients can still omit the field before decoding.
expect: The agent keeps the runtime boundary check because untyped external data enters there. It does not treat the internal required type as proof about external input.

input: A Python module has a function with no textual callers. The framework loads handlers from a configuration string, and the function name appears in that configuration.
expect: The agent searches configured and reflective uses before removal, finds the string entry point, and keeps the function. It does not equate no textual caller with dead code.

input: A JavaScript patch can shrink from twelve lines to four by joining statements with semicolons, using one-letter names, and nesting three conditional expressions. Tests would still pass.
expect: The agent rejects the rewrite as code golf. It does not claim formatting, packed statements, or short names as simplification, and it preserves the readable form.

input: Simplify the implementation changed by this task. The task diff edits a shared function used across several modules and changes behavior at an interface boundary. Review the code and make the smallest safe simplification.
expect: The response must inspect every module affected by the change, including callers, callees, side effects across call paths, and behavior at module or interface boundaries. It must not limit review scope to files or lines in the task diff. It must identify affected modules before proposing or applying a simplification and preserve their observed behavior. Fail responses that review only the task diff, even if the local edit is valid.

input: A changed TypeScript request handler has deeply nested checks. Guard clauses preserve behavior, make each rejection direct, and lower its measured complexity. The focused tests pass.
expect: The agent runs `rust-code-analysis-cli --metrics --output-format json --paths <file>` before the edit. It walks the JSON spaces tree to find the function record. It reduces the nested control flow because clarity improves. It runs the same command again and reports both function metrics with the focused test result. It does not add a helper only to lower the metric.

input: A changed TypeScript function has twelve flat match cases. The analyzer reports a cyclomatic-complexity score of 12. Each case is short, direct, and maps one protocol value to one result. Extracting helpers would only hide the cases. The focused tests pass.
expect: The agent reports the rust-code-analysis-cli function record as a review signal and keeps the flat match. It explains that the score stays high because the direct branches are clearer. It does not extract helpers or claim that a lower score is always better.

input: A changed function loops over n records. One section checks four fixed flags per record. Another section compares every record with all n records. No section allocates input-sized temporary storage.
expect: The agent analyzes the fixed-inner-bound section as O(n) time and the input-sized nested section as O(n squared) time. It analyzes auxiliary space as O(1) and does not classify nesting from syntax alone.

input: A changed function compares each of n customers with each of m independent rules and appends k matches to its result. It uses only scalar temporary values.
expect: The agent keeps n and m independent. It analyzes time as O(nm), returned output storage as O(k), and auxiliary space as O(1). It does not replace m with n.

input: For each of n queries, changed code scans m uniquely keyed catalog items. Output order follows query order. The supported runtime guarantees expected constant-time lookup and insertion for its map. Focused tests pass.
expect: The agent can replace the repeated scans with one map while preserving output order. It compares O(nm) time with expected O(n + m) time and records O(m) auxiliary space. It ties the expected bound to the runtime guarantee. Static proof is enough for the bound, but any practical benefit claim includes measurement.

input: A changed function transforms n input rows and returns a new n-row array. It keeps one temporary row during each iteration and no other growing storage.
expect: The agent analyzes O(n) time. It separates O(n) returned output storage from O(1) auxiliary space instead of reporting one undifferentiated space bound.

input: A changed merge routine recursively processes both halves, performs linear merge work, and reaches logarithmic call depth. Its supported library version documents worst-case O(n log n) stable sorting. The routine allocates an n-item merge buffer.
expect: The agent derives O(n log n) time from the recursion and O(log n) stack depth from live calls. It accounts for the O(n) merge buffer. It relies on the named library guarantee for sorting behavior and preserves stability.

input: A changed wrapper loops over n values and calls a vendor normalizer once per value. No documentation or implementation reveals the normalizer's time or temporary storage costs.
expect: The agent leaves the normalizer and total bounds unknown. It can identify n calls and known loop overhead, but it does not invent constant callee time or space.

input: A changed parser scans a configuration list whose enforced caller limit is eight items. A lookup table would add state and branching. Focused tests cover the limit and pass.
expect: The agent keeps the clear scan. It uses the enforced caller limit to find no work that scales with input and does not optimize a small bounded input without evidence of a practical problem.

input: Changed code copies n pending items, then repeatedly removes the first copied item. The supported array documentation makes each removal linear. A cursor over the private copy preserves order and visible behavior. Focused tests pass.
expect: The agent can replace front removal with cursor traversal. It reports O(n squared) time before and O(n) time after, with O(n) auxiliary space for the copy in both versions. Static evidence proves the bounds without a benchmark. It does not claim a practical speed or memory benefit without measurement.

input: A changed function needs cyclomatic-complexity evidence, but rust-code-analysis-cli is not installed. Focused tests pass, and the code also contains loops whose algorithmic bounds can be determined from the source and documented collection operations.
expect: The agent marks cyclomatic evidence unavailable and does not invent a score or other analyzer metrics. It requires the managed installer before the next pass. It still performs the independent static algorithmic review where the source and documented operation costs provide valid evidence.

input: A changed graph traversal uses an adjacency list. It visits each of V vertices once and, for each vertex, iterates only over that vertex's neighbors. Across all vertices, those dependent neighbor-list lengths sum to E. Focused tests pass.
expect: The agent sums the actual dependent inner bounds and analyzes total time as O(V + E). It rejects syntax-only multiplication into O(VE) and does not treat each neighbor loop as if it independently traversed all E edges.
